content.value_statement: Developers often need reliable Plotly examples for many chart types. This skill provides concise Python guidance for charts, styling, interactivity, exports, and Dash integration.
actual_capabilities: Choose between Plotly Express and graph_objects for a visualization task.
Create examples for scatter, line, bar, histogram, box, violin, heatmap, map, 3D, and financial charts.
Customize layouts, templates, colors, axes, legends, annotations, shapes, and hover behavior.
Export figures to HTML, PNG, PDF, SVG, browser, and notebook outputs.
Add rangesliders, range selectors, buttons, dropdowns, sliders, and animations.
Embed figures in Dash applications and Jinja2 templates.
limitations: It does not execute charts or verify rendered output by itself.
Static image export may require Kaleido and Chrome or Chromium.
Some map styles may require external tokens or internet access.
It focuses on Python Plotly, not JavaScript Plotly.js.

use_cases.title: Explore Data Quickly
use_cases.description: Create Plotly Express charts from pandas DataFrames for fast exploration and comparison.

use_cases.title: Prepare Research Figures
use_cases.description: Build publication-ready statistical, scientific, and 3D visuals with controlled styling and export formats.

use_cases.title: Prototype Dash Dashboards
use_cases.description: Embed interactive Plotly figures in Dash layouts for early dashboard prototypes and internal tools.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Chart
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Plotly Express to create a [chart type] from a pandas DataFrame named [df]. Explain the needed columns.

prompt_templates.title: Style and Export a Figure
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve my Plotly figure for a report. Add titles, labels, colors, hover text, and export options for [format].

prompt_templates.title: Build a Multi-Panel View
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Plotly subplot layout that compares [metrics] across [groups]. Include shared axes, legends, and clear annotations.

prompt_templates.title: Add Interactive Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Plotly design with dropdowns, range selectors, sliders, or animation for [dataset]. Explain when graph_objects is needed.

output_examples.input: Create a scatter plot with a trendline and hover labels.
output: Recommends Plotly Express for the first version.
Specifies x, y, color, trendline, and hover fields.
Suggests layout updates for title, axis labels, and tooltip clarity.

output_examples.input: Export a chart for a report and a web page.
output: Explains when to use PNG, PDF, SVG, or HTML.
Notes Kaleido requirements for static image export.
Describes standalone HTML and CDN-based HTML tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Compare Plotly Express and graph_objects for my chart.
output: Uses Plotly Express for standard charts with tidy data.
Uses graph_objects for mixed traces, custom shapes, and precise control.
Shows how both approaches can be combined in one figure.

best_practices: Start with Plotly Express, then use graph_objects methods for fine control.
Keep source data tidy and name DataFrame columns clearly before building figures.
Choose export settings based on target channel: HTML for exploration, SVG or PDF for publication.
anti_patterns: Do not embed sensitive data in shared HTML outputs.
Do not use CDN export settings when offline deployment is required.
Do not force graph_objects for simple charts that Plotly Express can create clearly.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps create Python Plotly charts, exports, interactivity, styling, and dashboard examples.

faq.question: Does it support Plotly Express?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Plotly Express guidance for quick charts with pandas DataFrames.

faq.question: Does it support graph_objects?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains graph_objects for custom traces, subplots, shapes, annotations, and advanced charts.

faq.question: Can it help with static image export?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers PNG, PDF, SVG, and related Kaleido export settings.

faq.question: Can it help with Dash?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes basic Dash integration for showing Plotly figures in web applications.

faq.question: Will it run my visualization code?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples, but execution depends on the local environment.
